Sections 498A/323/307/34 of the Indian Penal Code and  Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
 And

In the matter of : Nuresha Bibi  
 Ms. Sananda Bhattacharyya  ....For the Petitioner.
 Mr. B.K. Panda,
 Ms. Ayana De  ... For the State.

1. 
Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
2. The petitioner is the mother-in-law of the de facto complainant.

3. Considering the materials available in the case diary, the nature and extent of complicity of the petitioner in the commission of the alleged offence, the injury report and the role ascribed to the petitioner and also having regard to the fact that she is a lady and, moreover, the charge-sheet has already been filed, we are of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not necessary.
4.

Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest, the petitioner namely, Nuresha Bibi, shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.5,000/-, with two registered sureties of like amount each, to the satisfaction of the arresting officer and also subject to the conditions as laid down under Nuresha Bibi vs Unknown on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52647748/
1 Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C., 1973 corresponding to Section 482(2) of the BNSS, 2023.

Signed By :
GURUPADA CHAKRABARTY High Court of Calcutta 8 th of October 2024 02:21:31 PM 5.

It is further directed that the petitioner shall appear before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ghatal, Paschim Medinipur in connection with G.R. Case No.1122 of 2021 within two weeks from date.
